title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1LC1RC_0RA0LD_0LE1RE_0RF0LC_1RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1LC1RC_0RA0LD_0LE1RE_0RF0LC_1RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Both ends of the tape grow logarithmically. The left end is a long run of 10 after a few 0s (24 copies at step 556,283,168, 25 at step 1,678,517,170). The right end is a run of 110 (15 copies at step 1.8·109). In between lies a word of short digits (10, 110, 1110) in no fixed order that changes at each pass, like the digits of a counter, and decides when the head next reaches the left end. It is the same kind of machine as 1RB---_1LC1RF_0LE0RD_0RB0LC_1RD0LD_0RC0RA. No exact rule for the middle has been found.
verdict: The question is open. The machine can halt only from 1 C> 1 1 (both directions proved in Lean); in 20,000,000,000 steps that never happens. In the first 109 steps C had 1 C> 1 0 about 2.9·107 times and 0 C> 1 1 about 8.8·107 times, but never 1 C> 1 1: two of the three cells match all the time, the third never.

New, 14 November 2026. The whole run is now one rule: the tape is a binary counter with doublers (words 1010, 000, 100), and each round sends one defect through it. A tape with one defect cannot halt; a halt needs two defects to meet. In 100,000 rounds there was no halt, and in the 4,500 rounds followed word by word every defect disappeared long before the next one started. Whether that is always so is the open question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 273 cells have been visited and 135 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.054). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.074).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From 1 C> 1 1 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is F reading a 1. F is entered from A reading a 1 (moving left) or E reading a 0 (moving right). A is entered only from C reading a 0, which writes a 0 to A's left, so the first way is impossible. E is entered from D reading a 0 (moving left, and then F reads the 0 D wrote) or a 1 (moving right), so the halt needs D> 1 0 1; D is entered only from C reading a 1 and moving left, which gives 1 C> 1 1. Lean proves the steps from each context to the halt (halt_ctx, halt_ctx_A, halt_ctx_E). The argument backwards is checked in Lean too, by enumerating the cells the head reads: a configuration halts three steps later if and only if it is 1 C> 1 1 (halt_iff_3; one and two steps before a halt: halt_pred_1, halt_pred_2), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_3).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 8 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example B> (100)^n becomes (101)^n B> in 7n steps and (110)^n C> 1 becomes C> 1 (000)^n in 3n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 323 cells wide and holds 156 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: In the first 109 steps C had 1 C> 1 0 about 2.9·107 times and 0 C> 1 1 about 8.8·107 times, but never 1 C> 1 1: two of the three cells match all the time, the third never.

claims.title: Growth
claims.text: Both ends grow logarithmically; the visits to the left end come at exponentially spaced times.

claims.title: The contexts of C
claims.text: In 109 steps C has, around it, 0 C> 1 0 29,411,582 times, 0 C> 1 1 88,235,359, 1 C> 0 0 147,058,544, 1 C> 0 1 29,411,751, 1 C> 1 0 29,412,045 and 0 C> 0 0 22 times (last at step 556,283,163, at the left end); never 1 C> 1 1, the halting context.

claims.title: Runs on the tape
claims.text: In 300 tapes sampled every 1,000,003 steps up to 3·10<sup>8</sup>, the runs of 1s strictly inside the tape have length 1 to 3 (15,162, 2,509 and 4,013 runs). The runs of 0s are mostly of length 1 or 2 (17,602 and 2,089); of the longer ones, lengths 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11 are common (685, 707, 114, 293, 124, 151) and lengths 3, 6, 9, 12 rare (25, 7, 1, 1).

claims.title: No small finite-automata certificate
claims.text: A finite-automata-reduction search (a DFA of n states on one side of the head, the least co-closed NFA on (state × DFA state) + bottom for the other) finds no certificate with n ≤ 7 (23,836,540 DFAs at n = 7), with the DFA on the left or on the right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs C on a 1 with 1s on both sides, which the words of the tape have never offered; whether they never will depends on the counter in the middle, whose rule is not found.

claims.title: The run as rounds of one function
claims.text: For the twin 1RB0LE_0LC0RA_1LE0RD_0RB---_0LF0LD_1LA0LF (whose round words S_k appear on this machine's tape as 0 0 0 1 0 S_k at every second visit of E to a new leftmost cell, checked up to k = 18): on its mirrored tape, a visit of A (the head at a cell in state A until it first steps left of it) is a function on the half tape, and four such functions (A, E, F, P) close up. From [A] 0 0 S the machine returns to [A] 0 0 S' one cell further out with S' = 1 0 A(S). Derived by local simulation and checked against direct simulation of the machine.

claims.title: No halt in 100,000 rounds
claims.text: The visit engine, with visit counts kept as sums of powers of two, ran 100,000 rounds of the twin without a halt; the counts reach 187,512 bits. Only 7 window rules of A and E are ever used.

claims.title: A counter with doublers and one travelling defect
claims.text: In the words L = 1010, O = 000, I = 100 the function A is a binary counter (O, I the digits) in which every carry crossing an L becomes two. Each round adds one defect (a 10, 1 or 0 that does not fit the words), which travels through the counter, rewrites it, and disappears where it turns 1 I O into O L. Worked out by hand from the four functions: a tape with one defect cannot halt; a halt needs two defects side by side. The token rules reproduce the exact tape cell for cell (rounds 5 to 24), and in every round from 13 to 4,500 the defect disappeared about 40% of the way into the tape, long before the round ended.

claims.title: Does every defect disappear in time?
claims.text: If the defect of every round disappears before the round ends, the machine never halts. Where it disappears depends on the digits of the counter, which look irregular; no proof.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine has run 20,000,000,000 steps without stopping. Its tape is a slow counter with two ends: a long run of 10 on the left and runs of 110 on the right. It can stop only from one local pattern, 1 C> 1 1, which it has never produced.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 323 cells visited.
Every halt passes through it, and it always halts (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_iff_3).
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A counter with doublers and a travelling defect
html: Read the twin's tape (which this machine carries as 0 0 0 1 0 S at its left-end visits) in the words L = 1010, O = 000, I = 100. A visit of state A to a tape of such words is a counter step:
A(O W) = I W   A(I W) = O A(W)   A(L W) = L A(A(W))

O and I are binary digits, lowest first, and L is a doubler: a carry that crosses it becomes two carries. One round of the machine is S' = 1 0 A(S). The 1 0 put in front does not fit the words; it is a defect. Pushed by the carries, the defect travels through the counter, rewrites the words it crosses, and disappears where it turns 1 I O into O L, two digits into a doubler. Every round adds exactly four words.

A tape with one defect cannot halt (worked out by hand from the rules, not yet in Lean). A halt needs two defects side by side, so the machine runs forever if every defect disappears before the next round starts. In every round from 13 to 4,500 it did, about 40% of the way into the tape; the run of 100,000 rounds (visit counts up to 187,512 bits) has no halt. Where the defect disappears depends on the digits of the counter, which look irregular: that is what a proof would have to control.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.054). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.074).
After 109 steps the tape spans 273 cells (44 left of the start, 217 right), with a density of 1s of 0.495.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is F reading a 1. F is entered from A reading a 1 (moving left) or E reading a 0 (moving right). A is entered only from C reading a 0, which writes a 0 to A's left, so the first way is impossible. E is entered from D reading a 0 (moving left, and then F reads the 0 D wrote) or a 1 (moving right), so the halt needs D> 1 0 1; D is entered only from C reading a 1 and moving left, which gives 1 C> 1 1. Lean proves the steps from each context to the halt (halt_ctx, halt_ctx_A, halt_ctx_E). So the machine halts exactly when it produces 1 C> 1 1; Lean proves both directions (halt_ctx: the steps from there to the halt; halt_iff_3: nothing else halts three steps later).

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: Not known. Halting needs C on a 1 with 1s on both sides, which the words of the tape have never offered; whether they never will depends on the counter in the middle, whose rule is not found.

The basic moves are proved in Lean for every length (lean/Rules.lean: crossing a run of one word in a fixed number of steps per copy), so a proof would need only the rule of the counter on top of them.

sections.heading: Two cells out of three
html: The halt needs C on a 1 with a 1 on each side, 1 C> 1 1. In the first 109 steps C stood on a 1 with one of the two neighbours right 117 million times, never with both:

around Ctimes
0 C> 1 188,235,359
1 C> 1 029,412,045
0 C> 1 029,411,582
1 C> 1 10

A hint of the reason: runs of 0s of length 3, 6, 9 or 12 are rare on the tape while lengths 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11 are common, so the machine seems to keep track of lengths modulo 3. No automaton tried so far (finite automata reduction with up to 7 states) proves it.

summary: Binary counter with doublers (words 1010, 000, 100) and one travelling defect per round; a tape with one defect cannot halt; no halt in 100,000 rounds; open: that every defect disappears before the next round.
